Refactoring log

Source: REFACTORING-LOG.md

One bullet per commit, newest at the bottom: - YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM: plain-language one-liner. See the “Log every commit” rule in REFACTORING.md.

  • 2026-07-22 11:08: Added the refactoring brief (goal, rules, codebase conventions) and this commit log; renamed leftover “entity” wording to “definition” in a few comments.
  • 2026-07-22 12:05: Documented that a script observed-data source runs arbitrary R (security note on loadObservedData and in the vignette).
  • 2026-07-22 12:10: Warn once per session when a script observed-data source is sourced; moved rlang to a hard dependency.
  • 2026-07-22 12:14: Warn (instead of dropping silently) when a programmatic observed-data source has no data behind it.
  • 2026-07-22 12:18: On save, a programmatically added DataSet is now written to a PKML file so it survives a reload.
  • 2026-07-22 12:22: Updated the observed-data vignette and NEWS for the round-trip and the script-vs-programmatic safety trade-off.
  • 2026-07-22 12:35: Fixed a data-loss bug when saving a programmatic DataSet; the whole batch is validated before any PKML is written.
  • 2026-07-22 13:10: Addressed PR review on the observed-data work: keep a session DataSet recoverable if a save aborts, guard name-less and unsafe-named sentinels, warn per project, and align the log format with the rule.
  • 2026-07-22 14:30: Gave the parameter-set entry and parameter-identification add* functions a uniform overwrite policy: a duplicate now errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 14:45: Extended the overwrite policy to addOutputPath(): an existing id errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 15:10: Extended the overwrite policy to addIndividual(): an existing id errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 15:20: Extended the overwrite policy to addPopulation(): an existing id errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 15:30: Extended the overwrite policy to addApplication(): an existing id errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 15:45: Extended the overwrite policy to addParameterSet() and addInitialConditions(): an existing set id errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 16:00: Extended the overwrite policy to addScenario(): an existing id errors unless overwrite = TRUE (distinct from the overwriteFormulasInSS model option).
  • 2026-07-22 16:20: Extended the overwrite policy to addPlot(), addPlotGrid(), and addDataCombined(): an existing id errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 16:45: Extended the overwrite policy to addObservedData(): a source whose id (DataSet name or file basename) already exists errors unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • 2026-07-22 18:30: Addressed PR review on the overwrite policy: shared .assertNoOverwriteClash() helper + catalog message across the add* functions, warn when overwriting a referenced parameter/initial-condition set, attribute entry-add aborts to the public function, validate overwrite passed through ..., and make addObservedData() overwrite abort clearly on a file-based name collision without growing the name cache.
  • 2026-07-22 15:00: Unified R6 method and helper casing to camelCase: validationResult methods, Project’s parsing-era private methods, and the shared validation check helpers.
  • 2026-07-22 15:30: Dropped the severity/kind prefixes from messages catalog entry names (error/stop/warning/validation/message), naming each by what it describes; kept a short context qualifier where two entries would otherwise collide.
  • 2026-07-22 16:00: Normalized @family roxygen values to camelCase (spaced and kebab-case ones), leaving singular/plural as-is; updated the matching has_concept() entry in _pkgdown.yml.
  • 2026-07-23 11:34: Removed three unused test helpers (testProjectExcelConfigurationsPath, executeWithTestFile, createValidPISheets) from tests/testthat/helpers.R. (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 11:35: Removed orphan test fixtures unreferenced by any test (ObsDataAciclovir_1/2/3.pkml, ProjectConfiguration-V5.xlsx). (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 11:40: Merged the duplicated settings test file into test-esqlabs-env.R, keeping the exact esqlabsRSettingNames list check and the snapshot error test; removed test-esqlabsr-settings.R. (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 11:45: Switched the two sensitivity xlsx-write tests to withr::local_tempfile() so nothing is written into the package test directory and an early failure cannot orphan the file. (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 11:50: Converted all bare set.seed() calls in the sensitivity and plot/population test files to withr::local_seed(), so a test no longer leaks the session RNG state past its own block. (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 11:59: Added stopIfFails to runScenarios(), defaulting to abort when a scenario produces no results (#1036).
  • 2026-07-23 12:01: Extracted the shared scenario build loop into .buildScenarioSimulations(); runScenarios() now builds through it (prep for buildSimulations(), #1074).
  • 2026-07-23 12:05: Added exported buildSimulations() returning parameterized-but-unrun simulations per scenario (#1074).
  • 2026-07-23 12:08: Gave population entries an optional type (programmatic/csv): type-aware parse, validation, and a source-aware print (#1024).
  • 2026-07-23 12:11: addPopulation() now accepts an ospsuite::Population object (session injection), with a runtime store, accessor, and reload reset (#1024).
  • 2026-07-23 12:16: The run path resolves a population by its entry type (programmatic from the store, csv from its file, else demographics spec), scenario CSV flag kept for back-compat (#1024).
  • 2026-07-23 12:19: saveProject() freezes an injected Population to <id>.csv and rewrites its entry to a csv source, so it survives reload (#1024).
  • 2026-07-23 12:29: Addressed review: orphan programmatic population sentinel now serializes verbatim (no save-blocking abort); moved two run-path aborts to the messages catalog; shared the scenario build preflight (#1130).
  • 2026-07-23 14:20: Dropped three no-op local_seed() calls before summarizer() in the PK-parameter tidy-dataframe test; summarizer() is pure dplyr and consumes no RNG. (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 14:31: ponytail cleanup: inline single-use .asPopulation, shrink .populationEntryRequiredFields, fold .resolveProgrammaticPopulation into its switch arm (#1130).
  • 2026-07-23 14:45: Made the esqlabsRSettingNames test order-insensitive (set-equality on the names plus an enum-shape check) instead of asserting a fixed list order, since the names derive from an environment whose order is not guaranteed. (#1059)
  • 2026-07-23 15:06: PR review: narrow injected-population dispatch to a real Population object; clean up inline abort strings (#1024).
  • 2026-07-23 16:17: runScenarios()/buildSimulations() now canonicalize the scenarios argument before matching, so the name a scenario was authored with resolves to its canonical id (the same lowercasing/character-substitution ids get); a rewritten name warns. (#1157)
  • 2026-07-23 16:19: Canonicalize commas and interior spaces out of definition ids (filename-safe), fixing literal-comma parameter-set filenames on Excel import. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:22: addPITask()/PITask() can now create a task with no parameters or output mappings, so addPIParameter()/addPIOutputMapping() can seed the first one; a task left empty is flagged as a critical error by validateProject(). (#1157)
  • 2026-07-23 16:33: PIOutputMapping()/addPITask()/addPIOutputMapping() now accept either an output-path id or the literal model path of a defined output path for outputPath, resolving both to the id; the two divergent not-found aborts are unified into one message-catalog entry with a did-you-mean hint. (#1157)
  • 2026-07-23 16:37: NEWS entries for the three #1157 authoring-API ergonomics fixes. (#1157)
  • 2026-07-23 16:39: Excel import builds one application per protocol sheet for the 5.x one-sheet-per-protocol layout, so scenario application refs resolve. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:39: Excel multi-value cells parse the legacy quoted-CSV convention (strip quotes, keep a quoted comma in one token) alongside backslash escaping. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:42: Excel import defaults OverwriteFormulasInSS to FALSE when the Scenarios sheet omits the column, instead of aborting; a pre-6.0 sheet now imports. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:43: Excel import links an individual to its own override parameter-set sheet (matched by canonical id), so the override is applied instead of orphaned. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:51: addPopulation() / setPopulation() accept proteinOntogenies, matching individuals and the Excel importer, so an imported population can be re-authored. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:51: Excel import defaults a blank steady-state time/unit to 1000 / "min" (matching the authoring API), so a round-tripped project has no steady-state diff. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:55: Excel import reifies the configured dataFile as an excel observed-data definition (with its sheets and importer config), warning if the file is missing. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 17:03: Excel import parses the legacy 5.x parameter-identification layout (PITaskName-keyed sheets, no PITasks sheet), reassembling each task and resolving full-path output-mapping refs to output-path ids. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 17:08: Reconcile NEWS.md dev section for the Excel legacy-migration work (canonicalization char list, individual-sheet auto-link, new importer bullet). (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 16:41: Fixed the second buildSimulations unknown-name test to expect the canonicalized name in the error. (#1157)
  • 2026-07-23 17:57: PR review: dropped suppressWarnings on the runScenarios/buildSimulations canonicalization (a rewritten name now warns, surfacing a wrong-scenario match) and corrected the docs to say full canonicalization not just case; guarded .matchOutputPathRef against a non-scalar outputPath and hardened .nearestMatch so a NULL/multi-length value aborts with the typed message; aligned the addPITask outputPath-not-found error, addPITask roxygen, and NEWS wording. (#1157)
  • 2026-07-23 18:01: PR #1160 review: guard blank/NA cells in the 5.x Excel parsers (blank IndividualId, blank Parameter Name, boolean OptionValue) and keep an observed-data subfolder path. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-23 23:26: restoreProject() now detects a previous-version monolithic project snapshot (the single JSON from an older snapshotProjectConfiguration()) and upgrades it to the v6 tree by rebuilding the mirrored Excel workbooks and running them through importProjectFromExcel(); new R/import-legacy-snapshot.R plus a message-catalog entry and a fixture-driven test. (#1156)
  • 2026-07-23 23:52: PR #1161 review: legacy-snapshot upgrade now reads row cells by column name (not position), guards a malformed sheet with a clear abort, and basenames a populations-CSV filename so it cannot escape the target folder. (#1156)
  • 2026-07-24 00:20: PR #1161 review round 2: legacy-snapshot upgrade now muffles the redundant “data file not found” warning (was failing under testthat 3e), writes each workbook under the filename its projectConfiguration records (not a hardcoded name), keeps a zero-padded id column as text through type restoration, and emits the stale-handle warning on an overwriting restore like the v6 path. Classed the importer’s skipped-observed-data warning so it can be muffled. (#1156)
  • 2026-07-24 00:34: PR #1161 CodeRabbit: tighten .legacySheetToDf() sheet validation, a present-but-malformed rows (scalar or non-list record) now raises the clear malformed-sheet message instead of a cryptic indexing error; an absent rows stays a valid empty sheet. (#1156)
  • 2026-07-24 07:30: PR #1160 review: guard NULL before subsetting in .pi5xTaskRows(), so importing a legacy 5.x workbook missing optional PI sheets returns an empty frame instead of aborting. (#1158)
  • 2026-07-24 09:00: Gender is now optional on an individual, defaulting to UNKNOWN when absent (importer, addIndividual(), and the validator), so an animal species whose only valid PK-Sim gender is UNKNOWN can be represented and run. (#1162)
  • 2026-07-24 09:20: runScenarios() no longer crashes on an individual that carries no age/height; the missing biometric is passed through as NULL (which ospsuite defaults) instead of being coerced to a length-zero numeric. (#1162)
  • 2026-07-24 09:45: runScenarios(stopIfFails = FALSE) now also skips a scenario that fails at build time (was: only result collection was guarded, so a build failure aborted the whole batch); the broken scenario warns and collects as no-results while the rest run. buildSimulations() keeps its abort-on-failure contract. (#1170)
  • 2026-07-24 10:30: review fixes for the build-time-skip work: result collection no longer calls getAllQuantitiesMatching() on a skipped scenario’s NULL simulation; a skipped scenario’s slot is kept as an explicit NULL (single-bracket assignment) instead of being deleted, which had shortened the list and broken the run loops when a non-last scenario failed; runScenarios() docs and NEWS updated for the build-time skip; shared runSimulations no-results test mock. (#1170)
  • 2026-07-24 14:19: dataCombined validation now runs on the JSON spec directly via a dataCombined validation adapter (removed the legacy DataFrame reshape and the FromExcel validator); moved dataCombined shape validation out of the plots adapter so an error is no longer reported twice, and createDataCombined() / createPlots() pre-flight the dataCombined section so a bad definition aborts cleanly. (#1026)
  • 2026-07-24 14:19: addDataCombined() simulated entries accept an output-path id for path, resolved to the literal path when the DataCombined is built; dropping a missing-dataSet observed entry now also skips its transform. (#1042)
  • 2026-07-27 09:10: PR #1178 review: the gender-to-UNKNOWN default now also applies on the JSON-load path (.parseIndividuals()), so a hand-authored gender-less individual behaves like one from the authoring API or Excel; validateProject() flags a present-but-invalid gender token; a blank or whitespace-only Excel Gender cell counts as absent; and a scenario skipped at build time warns once instead of twice. (#1162, #1170)
  • 2026-07-27 09:40: The deprecated paramSheets argument now actually warns: the deprecation is raised in createScenariosFromPKML() itself instead of three layers down, where lifecycle could not tell the call came from a user and so stayed silent. Fixes the long-failing soft-deprecation test.
  • 2026-07-27 11:05: Excel import no longer loses a parameter set when two workbooks use the same sheet name. The workbook read first keeps the plain id, the later sheet is renamed, and the references that workbook makes (an individual’s own sheet, an application’s protocol sheet, their parameter-set columns) now follow the rename instead of quietly resolving to the other workbook’s set. A warning names each rename. (#1163)
  • 2026-07-27 11:20: An imported data combination no longer holds two spellings of one scenario: the observed block’s scenario reference is now lowercased to the canonical id the same way the simulated block’s already was. (#1165)
  • 2026-07-27 11:45: Importing an Excel project into a different folder now brings the referenced models, data, and population folders along, so the result actually runs instead of ending in File-Not-Found warnings. The results folder, an out-of-project folder, and an in-place import are left alone; a folder the configuration names but the Excel project lacks is reported. (#1164)
  • 2026-07-27 12:10: Importing an Excel project now says what it did (project written, definition counts per section, folders copied or missing) instead of finishing silently outside an interactive session. silent = TRUE turns it off. (#1166)
  • 2026-07-27 13:05: Review fixes for the import work: a ../-climbing folder value in the project configuration is no longer copied (it read outside the Excel project and wrote outside the output folder, overwriting whatever sat beside it), now contained the same way every other author-controlled path in the importer is; plus tests for the not-copied cases and two test comments reworded to describe the current behaviour rather than the old bug. (#1164)
  • 2026-07-27 13:15: addParameterEntry() now takes a missing unit the way a spreadsheet gives it: an NA cell, or no units argument at all, means the value is in a base unit instead of aborting. (#1167)
  • 2026-07-27 13:30: initProject() now creates the destination folder when it is missing instead of refusing to start, so the very first call of the authoring workflow no longer needs a dir.create() in front of it. (#1173)
  • 2026-07-27 14:05: A scenario’s simulation time can now be given the way it is usually held in R, as the numbers c(start, end, resolution), instead of only as the “0, 42, 48” string; a list gives one grid per scenario. Clearing the field no longer makes a later read of it return the time unit. (#1168)
  • 2026-07-27 14:45: An observed-data declaration can now carry an id, and that id names its file on disk and is what removes it, so observed data is filed by id like every other section instead of by the data file’s name (which produced the odd doubled .xlsx.json). Declarations without an id behave exactly as before. (#1172)
  • 2026-07-27 15:05: addObservedData() now spells out what its entry list must contain, per source type, and says that the file paths in it are relative to the project’s data folder, so the shape no longer has to be reverse-engineered from the error messages. (#1171)
  • 2026-07-27 15:30: PR #1179 review: a status check no longer copies the whole model/data tree (the internal Excel comparison imports with the new copyAssets = FALSE); overwrite now governs the asset folders too, so a file you placed in the output yourself is not replaced; the imported-in-place check resolves symlinks instead of comparing path spellings; a parameter-set reference that differs only in case now follows a rename; and the rename warning pluralizes correctly and no longer blames “an earlier workbook” when both sheets are in the same file. (#1163, #1164)
  • 2026-07-27 15:55: createScenariosFromPKML() takes the numeric simulation-time grid too, so all three ways of setting a scenario’s time now accept the same forms. (#1168)
  • 2026-07-27 16:10: The observed-data article now tells readers they can name a source themselves with an id, next to where it explains the two handles a source carries. (#1172)
  • 2026-07-27 17:20: PR #1180 review: an observed-data definition file whose id disagrees with its filename, or whose id is not a string, now fails the load with the file named, instead of being silently re-filed on the next save or crashing somewhere else entirely. Adding a source rejects an unusable id up front, spots a clash with a hand-chosen id from either direction, and refuses to overwrite a session DataSet with a configuration entry (which would have stranded the data). (#1172)
  • 2026-07-27 17:30: PR #1180 review: documentation follow-ups. addObservedData() says that overwriting only replaces a source of the same kind, the definitions folder is described as the default layout rather than a fixed path, createScenariosFromPKML() no longer claims the time unit is used only when a time grid is supplied, and the observed-data article’s removal section mentions the declared id. (#1171, #1172)
  • 2026-07-28 09:40: A notes, scratch or fit-bounds sheet sitting beside the parameter sheets of a parameter workbook no longer stops an Excel import: the importer now tells a parameter sheet from any other by its columns and skips the rest with a warning, and a skipped sheet no longer leaves an application or an individual pointing at a parameter set that was never created. (#1181)
  • 2026-07-28 10:05: The rule that a path naming an environment variable is allowed to point outside the project now lives in one place, instead of the same pattern being spelled out at each of the three checks that apply it.
  • 2026-07-28 10:35: A project whose observed data sits on a synced drive outside the project folder now migrates: the Excel import says the data is out of reach and carries on, instead of refusing the whole project, and a data folder written as an environment variable is resolved rather than taken literally. (#1182)
  • 2026-07-28 11:10: PR #1188 review: a parameter workbook sheet whose name contains curly braces no longer crashes the import that was meant to tolerate it, and a data file that sits outside the data folder is now told so, instead of being told it is outside the project when it usually is not. (#1181, #1182)
  • 2026-07-28 11:25: PR #1188 review: a folder path written as $PATH/... no longer skips the check that keeps a project’s folders inside the project. $PATH is the one variable the package deliberately never substitutes, so such a path stays literal and was escaping unchecked. (#1182)
  • 2026-07-28 11:50: PR #1188 review: printing a project whose data folder sits outside the project (a synced drive) now shows that folder instead of failing, so a freshly imported project can be inspected. Reading the folder still refuses it, and a folder written as an unset environment variable prints as the variable. (#1182)
  • 2026-07-28 12:10: PR #1188 review: a data folder written as an environment variable that stands for a path inside the project is now resolved against the project file and copied along with it, so the folder found while importing is the folder found when the project is later opened. A variable that is not set is reported instead of passed over silently. (#1182)
  • 2026-07-28 12:35: PR #1188 review: when a sheet is skipped for not being a parameter sheet, an application or individual whose parameter-set column named it now loses that reference too, rather than keeping a pointer to something that was never created. The four column names that define a parameter sheet are written down once and read by both the Excel reader and the importer. (#1181)
  • 2026-07-28 13:05: A blank cell, or a missing column, in a legacy parameter-identification sheet no longer stops a project from being imported or restored. The four places that tested a cell for emptiness in a way that broke on an absent one now share a single test that handles it. (#1190)
  • 2026-07-28 13:35: Rows that are empty in every column are now ignored when a spreadsheet is read, so the trailing empty rows an Excel file picks up over years of editing are no longer taken for definitions with a missing name. A row that is empty in only some columns is still read as before. (#1191)
  • 2026-07-28 15:10: Two small shared pieces for the Excel reader: one test for “this cell has to be a number”, and one place that emits an import warning safely when the warning quotes text a modeller wrote. No change in behaviour.
  • 2026-07-28 15:40: A parameter row whose value cell holds text instead of a number is now skipped, with a warning naming its sheet, row and cell, instead of stopping the whole import. A fit-bounds sheet copied from a real parameter sheet no longer blocks a project’s migration. A blank value cell still means “no value”, as before. (#1189)
  • 2026-07-28 16:15: A parameter-identification sheet from before the output-path column existed can now be imported. Such a sheet named its outputs through the scenario, so each row is turned into one mapping per output path its scenarios list, keeping the rest of the row. A row whose scenarios list no output path is skipped with a warning instead of blocking the whole restore. (#1192)
  • 2026-07-28 16:50: Importing a project now says which data combinations have an observed curve with no data set named, and that the project will not pass its own check until that cell is filled. The rows are kept as authored rather than dropped, so the missing piece can still be supplied. The three warnings about observed data that could not be imported say the same thing. (#1183)
  • 2026-07-28 17:30: Review round on the import fixes: a skipped parameter row is now reported at the row Excel shows rather than a count that ignores blank rows; a sheet whose every row was skipped no longer becomes an empty parameter set; the parameter-identification derivation matches a scenario however it is spelled and skips a row that names no data set, which would otherwise have failed a moment later; and the note about a blank output-path cell now says what actually happens. (#1183, #1189, #1192)
  • 2026-07-28 18:05: A project whose parameter-identification mapping names no output path or no observed data now opens, and the project check reports it, instead of the load stopping. A workbook with one such blank cell was impossible to open and so impossible to fix. Creating such a mapping by hand is still refused. (#1192)
  • 2026-07-29 09:20: A project whose parameter-identification parameter has no path or is missing a bound now opens too, matching the output mappings, so a spreadsheet with one blank bounds cell can be opened and fixed. Every gap in a task is now listed in one report, because the missing-field checks moved to the section check, which is not skipped the way the cross-reference check is. (#1192)
